texts.title: Learning to swim as an adult

paragraphs.text: Many adults never learned to swim as children, and some feel embarrassed about starting later in life. Swimming pools increasingly offer lessons only for adults, often in the evening, when there are fewer people in the water.

The first lessons usually take place in shallow water and focus on breathing and floating rather than swimming strokes. Instructors say that learning to put the face in the water and breathe out slowly is the biggest step for most beginners.
Once learners feel relaxed, they are taught to kick with their legs while holding a float. Arm movements are added later, and most adults can swim a width of the pool after about ten lessons.
Fear is the most common obstacle. Instructors recommend setting small goals, such as floating for five seconds, and practising between lessons during quiet times at the pool.
Some pools also offer courses for adults who can swim but want to improve their technique or build fitness. These classes often include video recordings, so that swimmers can see how they move.
